subject: Prompt acceptance and canary backstop plan for Acme pilot
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Prompt acceptance and canary backstop plan for Acme pilot

Team —

Acme goes live with the pilot next month and wants us to run a short canary against the production intent distribution. I attached the prompt-suite_v1 and a suggested metrics workbook. I want to lock down:

- Concrete acceptance criteria for the prompt-suite A/B (what passes as a safe launch)
- Canary length and sample size
- Backstop thresholds that trigger an automatic fallback to the current model variant

Initial thoughts (please critique):
- Primary metric: task-success (binary pass rate) on the Acme validation set — target delta vs baseline <= -1.0 percentage point (i.e., no more than a 1pp drop).
- Safety metric: rate of hallucination flags (human audit) <= 0.5% absolute increase.
- UX metric: median response latency < 600ms at 99th pct for canary traffic.

Proposed canary: 1000 sessions over 72 hours routed via feature-flagged traffic (10% of Acme's live). If any one threshold is breached persistently over two sampling windows (24h), the route falls back to the baseline model and we open a regression ticket.

Please review and call out gaps. Marissa, can you confirm the auditing cadence and sampling? Karthik — can infra support a 24h rolling alarm that flips the route automatically? Priyom — what acceptance language should go in the pilot SOW so Acme understands the rollback/fallback behavior?

Attachments: prompt-suite_v1.jsonl (prompt examples + scoring rubric), canary-metrics.xlsx (calc sheets), proposal-rollout-timeline.pdf

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt acceptance and canary backstop plan for Acme pilot

Thanks — nice baseline. A few quick items from QA/op: 

- Sampling: we should seed the canary with a stratified sample to preserve high/low prompt complexity. 1000 sessions is fine but split across three strata (simple/medium/complex).
- Audit cadence: human review of 200 items per 24h window (random sample + edge-case focused). If human audit flags exceed 3% of the sampled items in a window, treat as a safety breach.
- Drift check: add a semantic-drift classifier to raise an alert if the embedding-space centroid shifts by > 0.07 cosine average vs baseline.

Owner suggestions: QA lead (Marissa) for audit runs; Applied ML (Priyom) for drift classifier; Infra (Dev) for alarm automation.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Quality Engineering

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-23T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt acceptance and canary backstop plan for Acme pilot

On Mon, Aug 22, 2027 at 09:15 AM Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed canary: 1000 sessions over 72 hours routed via feature-flagged traffic (10% of Acme's live). If any one threshold is breached persistently over two sampling windows (24h), the route falls back to the baseline model and we open a regression ticket.

We can automate the rule in the routing plane. Implementation notes: 
- We will evaluate windows in 6h buckets and apply a 24h moving average to avoid blips. Alert -> automatic fallback requires two conditions: (1) moving average breach, and (2) a secondary manual confirmation flag within 2h from on-call (can be a UI click). This prevents automatic flips on noisy metrics.
- Metric thresholds: agree with Aisha's task-success and Marissa's audit rules but tweak tolerances for the pilot: task-success delta <= -1.5pp (pilot tolerance), hallucination audit <= 0.8% absolute increase. If either is exceeded for two consecutive 24h windows -> trigger fallback.
- We will also capture full KV cache snapshots at start/end of the canary to help reproduce any model-state issues.

Dev: can you wire the 6h metric roll-ups into the routing alarm topic? Priyom: please prepare the drift-check model and a short runbook for triage.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Infrastructure

From: Emily Park <emily@acmedata.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt acceptance and canary backstop plan for Acme pilot

Forwarded message
From: Emily Park <emily@acmedata.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 24, 2027 at 08:40 AM
Subject: Re: Prompt acceptance and canary backstop plan for Acme pilot

Aisha — thanks for the detailed plan. Acme is broadly supportive but would like the canary stretched to 120 hours (to capture low-volume business hours) and to increase the sample to 1,500 sessions. Is that feasible without changing the acceptance thresholds? We understand fallbacks are automatic but request a one-hour hold window before the final fallback for our on-call to triage and comment.

Emily Park
Head of Product, Acme Data
emily@acmedata.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily@acmedata.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt acceptance and canary backstop plan for Acme pilot (finalized)

Thanks everyone — summary and decisions: 

- Canary scope: 1,500 sessions over 120 hours (stratified simple/medium/complex).
- Acceptance thresholds: task-success delta <= -1.5pp (pilot tolerance); hallucination audit <= 0.8% absolute increase; median latency < 600ms at 99pct.
- Alarm logic: 6h buckets, 24h moving average; fallback if threshold breached for two consecutive 24h windows. We will implement a 1-hour hold before final fallback so Acme can triage (per their ask).
- Owners: Marissa (QA audit), Priyom (drift classifier + scoring), Karthik/Dev (routing alarm + KV snapshot), Aisha (pilot coordinator + SOW language).
- Docs & links: prompt-suite_v1.jsonl (as attached), canary-metrics.xlsx live on Drive: https://redwood.app/s/drive/Acme-prompt-suite

Action items: 
1) Priyom to deliver drift-check model and runbook by 2027-08-30.
2) Dev to wire metric roll-ups into the routing topic and demo the 1-hour hold flow by 2027-09-01.
3) Marissa to start audit sampling plan and QA checklist by 2027-08-28.
4) Aisha to update pilot SOW with fallback language and circulate to Legal by 2027-08-27.

If no objections, I'll update the SOW and push the canary schedule to Acme.

Aisha
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
